text: Northwind employees on a hybrid schedule work from the office at least two days per week. Teams choose their anchor days with their manager and record them in the team calendar. Fully remote arrangements are approved case by case by the department head and reviewed every twelve months.

To set up a home workspace, each hybrid or remote employee may claim a one-time home office stipend of $500 for a desk, chair, monitor, or headset. Receipts must be submitted within 60 days of purchase. Laptops and docking stations are issued by IT and are not covered by the stipend.

Working from another country for more than two weeks requires written approval from your manager. Employees remain responsible for local tax and visa requirements, and company equipment may not be taken to embargoed countries.

Northwind employees on a hybrid schedule work from the office at least three days per week, with Tuesday and Thursday fixed as company-wide anchor days. Fully remote arrangements are approved by the department head and the VP of People, and are reviewed every six months.

Each hybrid or remote employee may claim a home office stipend of $750, renewable every three years, for a desk, chair, monitor, or headset. Receipts must be submitted within 30 days of purchase. Laptops and docking stations are issued by IT and are not covered by the stipend.

Working from another country for any length of time requires approval from your manager and the Legal team, requested at least 21 days before travel. Stays are limited to 30 days per calendar year, and company equipment may not be taken to embargoed countries.

Expense reports must be submitted in Expensify within 45 days of the expense date. Reports older than 90 days are rejected unless the finance controller grants an exception. Each line item needs an itemized receipt for amounts of $25 or more.

While travelling for work, meals are reimbursed up to a daily allowance of $60 within the United States and $80 internationally. Alcohol is not reimbursable unless a client is present and a senior manager approves it in advance.
Software subscriptions, conference registrations, and any single purchase above $1,000 require pre-approval from your cost-center owner before the money is spent.

Expense reports must be submitted in Ramp within 30 days of the expense date. Reports older than 60 days are rejected automatically. Each line item needs an itemized receipt for amounts of $75 or more; smaller items need a short business purpose.
While travelling for work, meals are reimbursed up to a daily allowance of $75 within the United States and $95 internationally. Alcohol is never reimbursable, including at client dinners.

Software subscriptions must go through IT procurement and cannot be expensed. Conference registrations and any single purchase above $500 require pre-approval from your cost-center owner before the money is spent.

Book all flights and hotels through Navan so that bookings appear on the duty-of-care map. Hotel rates are capped at $250 per night in tier-one cities such as New York, San Francisco, and London, and $180 per night elsewhere. Meals during travel follow the expense policy.

Economy class is the default for all flights. Premium economy is allowed on flights longer than six hours, and business class only for flights over ten hours with VP approval. Ride-share is preferred over rental cars for trips shorter than three days.

Passwords for company accounts must be at least 14 characters and are stored in 1Password. Passwords are not rotated on a schedule; they are changed immediately if a compromise is suspected. Every account must have hardware-key or authenticator-app MFA.

Report a lost or stolen laptop to the IT service desk within one hour, even outside business hours. IT will remotely lock and wipe the device. Delaying the report beyond 24 hours is treated as a security incident.

Customer data classified as Confidential may only be stored in approved systems: Salesforce, the production database, and the restricted Google Drive. It may never be pasted into personal email, chat tools outside Slack, or public AI assistants.
Phishing attempts should be reported with the Report Phish button in Gmail rather than forwarded. Clicking a phishing link is not a disciplinary matter if it is reported right away.
